_about.purpose: Hand-labelled queries for SupportCrew's optional evaluation mode. Each item is labelled with the EXPECTED behaviour so catch rate can be reported alongside false-positive rate. Labels are ground truth the human defines, not measured results.
_about.verify_before_use: The 'catch' cases assume the model answers from stale memory while the live web has the current answer. This depends on the model's training cut-off and on what is actually true on the web at build time. VERIFY each catch case when you build: confirm the model's likely answer is genuinely outdated and that a web search returns the corrected fact. Adjust or replace any case that no longer holds.

categories.catch: Model memory is likely stale; web should correct it. Expect contradiction_found=true, severity=material.
categories.control: Model is reliably correct on stable info. Expect contradiction_found=false (measures false-positive rate).
categories.refusal: Unanswerable without private/account data. Expect the closed-fail refusal (low confidence).

scoring.catch_rate: share of 'catch' cases where Agent 3 returned contradiction_found=true AND severity='material'
scoring.false_positive_rate: share of 'control' cases where Agent 3 wrongly returned contradiction_found=true
scoring.refusal_correct: share of 'refusal' cases where resolved_answer was the refusal string / confidence < 0.60

items.query: What is the latest stable version of Python?
items.rationale: Version advances over time; a model answering from memory may name an older release than the current stable one on python.org.

items.query: What is the latest Ubuntu LTS release?
items.rationale: A new LTS ships every two years (April of even years); a model with a 2023 cut-off names 22.04 while ubuntu.com lists the current LTS.
items.replaced: 2026-09-20: replaced 'current monthly price of ChatGPT Plus' — in the first run the model's remembered price ($20) was still current, so the stale-memory premise did not hold and the case could not produce a catch.

items.query: What is the newest iPhone model available right now?
items.rationale: A new flagship ships roughly yearly; memory likely lags the current model.

items.query: What is the current Long-Term Support (LTS) version of Node.js?
items.rationale: LTS lines rotate on a schedule; the model may name a superseded LTS.

items.query: What are the current free-tier limits for the OpenAI API?
items.rationale: Provider limits/policies change; memory is prone to stating outdated terms.

items.query: What is the latest version of the CrewAI framework?
items.rationale: Fast-moving library; the current release on PyPI likely differs from memory.

items.query: How do I reset my password?
items.rationale: Generic, stable procedure (the spec's own example); the direct answer should be fine and the web should not contradict it.
Stable definitional concept; no contradiction expected.

items.query: What does an HTTP 404 status code mean?
items.rationale: Stable technical fact; direct answer reliable.

items.query: What are some tips for creating a strong password?
items.rationale: Well-established guidance; web should broadly agree.

items.query: What is a VPN and what is it used for?
items.rationale: Stable definitional concept; no contradiction expected.

items.query: How do I clear the cache in a web browser?
items.rationale: Broadly stable procedure; minor UI wording differences should not rise to a material contradiction.
Account-specific; no public web truth exists. Expect the closed-fail refusal.

items.query: What is the current balance in my account?
items.rationale: Private data; unanswerable without authentication. Expect refusal.

items.query: When exactly will my refund be processed?
items.rationale: Depends on a specific account/transaction; not web-verifiable. Expect refusal.

items.query: Is the warranty on my specific device still valid?
items.rationale: Requires private purchase details; not answerable from the web. Expect refusal.
